signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-08-31 mobile-native-kmp create-listing nav wiring)
evidence: Navigation.kt:493 (composable(Screen.CreateListing.route)) hardwires CreateListingScreen's onSubmit to `{ _ -> Result.failure(NotImplementedError("Wire to listing API")) }`. This is a reachable production nav-graph path, not a test/stub module — a realtor navigating MyListings -> CreateListing and submitting the form ALWAYS gets a guaranteed failure. The realtor Create-Listing feature is dead end-to-end despite the UI being fully built.

CreateListingScreen.kt is a complete implementation, not a placeholder: onSubmit: suspend (CreateListingInput) -> Result<Unit> (:41), full form + validation + footer, and a real submit handler (:105-127) that sets isSubmitting, awaits onSubmit(...), then result.fold(onSuccess = { onCreated() }, onFailure = { ... }). Because onSubmit can only ever return the injected NotImplementedError failure, onCreated() (navigate back to MyListings, Navigation.kt:494) is unreachable and the user only ever sees the onFailure error branch.

The backing repository already exists and is used elsewhere in the SAME file: PortalListingsRepository (Navigation.kt:471 listMyListings, plus getPortfolioAnalytics referenced ~:498). So this is not a missing-backend gap — the create call simply was never wired to the repository. Fix: replace the NotImplementedError lambda with a real suspend call into PortalListingsRepository.create*(input) returning its Result, mirroring the listMyListings/onSuccess/onFailure pattern already in the file.

Confidence high: the failure is unconditional and statically traced from the nav-graph wiring (Navigation.kt:493) through the screen's fold (CreateListingScreen.kt:120-127) — no runtime state can make onSubmit succeed. Severity medium (+2): a whole realtor feature is non-functional on a user-facing path, but it fails closed with a handled error rather than crashing.
